hostKey.newExplain: This is the first time connecting to {{host}}. Check that the fingerprint below matches the server's before trusting it.
hostKey.changedWarning: The key presented by {{host}} does not match the one you trusted before. Someone could be intercepting your connection (man-in-the-middle), or the server was reinstalled. Only continue if you have verified the new fingerprint with the server's administrator.
hostKey.otherTypeKnown: You already trust a {{type}} key for this host; the server now offers a different key type.

keys.empty: No keys yet. Generate a new key or import an existing one.
keys.label: Label
keys.labelFromComment: Defaults to the key's comment or file name
keys.typeHint: ED25519 is fast, secure and widely supported. Use RSA only for very old servers.
keys.commentHint: Stored in the public key, e.g. who or what the key is for.
keys.importFormats: OpenSSH, PEM/PKCS#8 and PuTTY .ppk (v2 and v3) are supported. Keys are stored encrypted on this device.
keys.passphraseHint: Needed once to decrypt the key for import.
keys.needPassphrase: This key is protected by a passphrase.
keys.duplicate: This key is already in your keychain as “{{label}}”.
keys.publicKeyHint: Add this line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on a server to allow this key to log in.
keys.unused: Not used by any host, group or identity.
keys.exportExplain: Saves the private key (OpenSSH format) and the matching .pub file.
keys.exportPassphraseHint: Recommended. Uses aes256-ctr + bcrypt, like ssh-keygen.
keys.exportUnencryptedWarning: Without a passphrase, anyone who gets the exported file can use this key.
keys.deleteMessage: “{{label}}” will be deleted from this device. This can't be undone.
keys.deleteInUse: “{{label}}” is used by: {{users}}. They will stop using it. This can't be undone.

error.unsupported: This key type or format isn't supported.
error.invalid: This doesn't look like a valid private key.
error.integrity: The key file is corrupted or was modified.

forwards.title: Port forwarding
forwards.empty: Tunnel ports through SSH: reach a database behind a server (local), expose a local service on the server (remote), or browse through the server with a SOCKS proxy (dynamic).
forwards.label: Name

kindHint.local: Listen on this computer; connections go to a destination reachable from the server (ssh -L).
kindHint.remote: Listen on the server; connections come back to a destination reachable from this computer (ssh -R).
kindHint.dynamic: A SOCKS4/5 proxy on this computer; apps choose any destination via the server (ssh -D).

forwards.destRemote: Destination host (as seen from the server)
forwards.destLocal: Destination host (as seen from this computer)
forwards.exposedWarning: This listens on a non-loopback address, so other machines on the network can use the tunnel.

error.addrInUse: That port is already in use on this computer.
error.addrDenied: Not allowed to listen on that port (ports below 1024 may need admin rights).
error.addrNotAvail: That listen address doesn't exist on this computer.
error.remoteRefused: The server refused to listen on that address/port (check AllowTcpForwarding / GatewayPorts).
error.disconnected: The SSH connection for this tunnel was lost.

sshConfig.groupHint: Leave empty to import without a group.
sshConfig.importKeys: Import IdentityFile keys into Keys (unencrypted keys only; encrypted ones are listed)

lock.title: chh is locked
lock.startupHint: Your local data is encrypted with your master password.
lock.passwordHint: Enter your master password to continue.
lock.biometricFailed: Not verified. Use your passcode instead.
lock.tooManyAttempts: Too many attempts. Try again in {{seconds}} s.
lock.forgotMaster: Forgot it? The data on this device can't be recovered without it. If you use sync, reinstall and sign in to get your synced data back.
lock.screenHint: Hide chh behind a passcode after inactivity or when your computer sleeps. Connections keep running while locked.
lock.lockOnSleep: Lock when the computer sleeps or its screen locks
lock.masterHint: Encrypts this device's database key with a password you enter every time chh starts. Without it, nobody can read your local data, even with full access to your files.
lock.masterOn: A master password protects this device.
lock.masterWarning: If you forget the master password, the data on this device is lost. Synced data can be restored by signing in again.
lock.masterEnabled: Master password set. You'll be asked for it next time chh starts.

sync.intro: Sync keeps hosts, groups, keys, identities, known hosts, snippets and forwarding rules up to date across your devices. Everything is encrypted on this device with your password before upload; the server can't read it. Run your own server with the included Docker Compose setup.
sync.insecureHint: Plain HTTP is only allowed on local/private networks. Your data stays end-to-end encrypted, but sign-in tokens are not.
sync.passwordHint: At least 10 characters. It never leaves this device.
sync.totpHint: 6-digit code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code.
sync.zeroKnowledgeWarning: Your password encrypts your data. The server can't reset it. Keep the recovery key you'll be shown next somewhere safe.
sync.recoveryHint: If you forget your password, this key is the only way to get your synced data back. Store it offline, e.g. in a password manager or on paper.

state.offline: Offline: changes will sync when you're back online

sync.notSignedIn: Sync is off: open Sync settings
sync.twoFactorHint: Require a code from an authenticator app when signing in on a new device.
sync.scanHint: Scan the QR code with an authenticator app, or enter this key manually, then type the 6-digit code.
sync.qr: QR code for your authenticator app
sync.recoveryCodesHint: Save these one-time recovery codes. Each lets you sign in once if you lose your authenticator.
sync.passwordChanged: Password changed. Other devices need to sign in again.
sync.keepData: Keep my data on this device

advanced.title: Advanced connection
advanced.engineBuiltinHint: Built-in client with chh's keys, identities, known hosts, proxies and SFTP.
advanced.engineOpensshHint: Runs your installed `ssh` in the terminal: supports FIDO2 security keys and post-quantum key exchange; uses OpenSSH's own known_hosts and ~/.ssh/config. Passwords are typed in the terminal.
advanced.identityFileHint: e.g. a FIDO2 key handle created with ssh-keygen -t ed25519-sk.
advanced.jumpHostsHint: Connect through these hosts in order (nearest first). Each one uses its own login settings.
advanced.proxyUserHint: Optional; you'll be asked for the password.
advanced.agentForwardingHint: Lets the server use your local SSH agent (e.g. for git on the server). Only enable for servers you trust.
advanced.envHint: Set for the session. Group and host variables are combined.

skipped.protocol: Skipped: Telnet and serial hosts can't run commands non-interactively

ai.title: AI command suggestions (optional)
ai.hint: Ask an AI model for command suggestions from the Ctrl+Space list. Off by default and never automatic. Works with any OpenAI-compatible API, including local models (Ollama, llama.cpp).
ai.endpointHint: e.g. https://api.example.com/v1 or http://localhost:11434/v1 (local only over http).
ai.keyHint: Optional for local models. Stored encrypted on this device.
ai.sendHistory: Include my last 10 commands on that host as context
ai.privacy: Only sent when you ask: the current command line and the host's OS. Never passwords, keys, environment variables or terminal output.
ai.privacyWithHistory: Only sent when you ask: the current command line, the host's OS and your last 10 commands there. Never passwords, keys, environment variables or terminal output.

error.aiOff: AI suggestions are turned off (Settings → Terminal).
error.aiUrl: Use an https:// endpoint (http only for localhost).

cloud.hint: Instances become hosts. Importing again updates addresses (e.g. after a restart) instead of creating duplicates. Credentials are only used for this request and aren't stored.
cloud.keysHint: Overrides the profile. Use a read-only key (ec2:DescribeInstances).
cloud.doTokenHint: A read-only personal access token from the DigitalOcean control panel.
cloud.awsUserHint: Depends on the image: ec2-user (Amazon Linux), ubuntu, admin (Debian)…

error.forbidden: Access denied: the credentials need permission to list instances.

fido.title: Security keys (FIDO2 / YubiKey)
fido.hint: Hardware security keys keep the private key on the device and need a touch to log in. chh uses your system OpenSSH (8.2+) for them.
fido.useIt: Then add the .pub file's line to the server's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, and in the host's Advanced connection settings choose “System OpenSSH” and set the identity file.

teams.title: Teams
teams.needSync: Teams share hosts, identities, keys and snippets with other people through your sync server, end-to-end encrypted. Sign in to sync to create or join a team.
teams.empty: No teams yet. Create one, or ask a team admin to invite your account email.
teams.createExplain: A team has its own encrypted vault. Its name and everything in it are encrypted with a team key that only confirmed members hold.
teams.name: Team name
teams.awaitingConfirm: You joined this team. An admin now has to confirm you before you can see its items.
teams.awaitingConfirmHint: They will compare your key fingerprint with you. Yours is: {{fingerprint}}
teams.rotateNeededHint: Someone left or was removed without a key rotation, so they may still hold the current team key. Rotate it to protect future changes.
teams.rotateMessage: Every item in the team vault is re-encrypted with a new key, which is shared with the current confirmed members only. This can take a moment for large teams.
teams.leaveMessage: Items shared in {{name}} are removed from this device. An admin can invite you again later.
teams.deleteMessage: {{name}} and every item in its vault are deleted for all members. This cannot be undone. The audit log is kept on the server.
teams.removeRotateMessage: {{email}} is removed and the team key is rotated, so they can no longer decrypt anything that changes from now on. Items they already synced may remain on their devices.
teams.inviteHint: They accept in the Teams screen after signing in to this server with that email. No email is sent: let them know yourself.
teams.rolesHelp: Owner and admins manage members. Editors can change items. Viewers can use shared hosts but not change them.
teams.confirmExplain: Confirming shares the team key with this member's account.
teams.confirmWhere: Ask them to read out the fingerprint shown at the bottom of their Teams screen and check that it matches exactly. A mismatch means the key didn't come from them.
teams.confirmChecked: The fingerprint matches what they told me
teams.readOnlyHost: This host belongs to a team where you're a viewer, so you can't change it.
teams.vaultFieldHint: Hosts in a team vault are shared with its members.

move.title: Move “{{label}}”
move.explain: Moving re-encrypts the item for the vault you choose.
move.noTargets: There is no other vault you can move this to.
move.toTeamHint: All members of the team will see it. Linked items (its group, identity or key) aren't moved: move them too if teammates need them.
move.toPersonalHint: It is removed from the team for everyone else.

audit.explain: Everything members do with the team is recorded on the server. Entries marked “reported by app” come from members' apps; a modified app could skip them.
audit.clientReportedHint: Reported by the member's app, not observed by the server.

error.notSignedIn: Sign in to sync to use teams.
error.notConfirmed: An admin has to confirm you first.
error.fingerprintMismatch: The member's key changed since you compared it. Compare the new fingerprint before confirming.

teams.myFingerprintHint: Admins compare this with you before sharing a team key.
